examDifficulty.heading: Is the Development Lifecycle and Deployment Architect Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: The Dev Lifecycle and Deployment Architect exam is challenging because it tests hands-on operational knowledge — not just theory. You need to know sandbox types, their refresh intervals, deployment tool trade-offs, and how to design a CI/CD pipeline that handles destructive changes, test coverage requirements, and dependency ordering. Candidates with real deployment experience have a significant advantage.
bullets: 60 questions in 120 minutes — many questions describe a deployment scenario and ask you to select the correct tool, sandbox type, or sequencing approach.
~68% passing score — about 41 correct answers needed, with questions that test nuanced differences between change sets, Salesforce CLI, and unlocked packages.
Operational depth — expect questions on destructive changes, deployment dependency ordering, and how to handle failed production deployments without built-in rollback.
CI/CD pipeline design — the exam tests your ability to design automated pipelines using scratch orgs, version-controlled source, and package-based deployment.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Book the exam when you have hands-on experience with Salesforce CLI deployments, can explain the trade-offs between change sets and unlocked packages, and have designed at least one sandbox promotion strategy.

examFormat.heading: Development Lifecycle and Deployment Architect Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online or in-person. Here is the format:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Questions present deployment and release management scenarios, asking you to choose the right combination of sandbox type, deployment tool, and governance process for each situation.
bestWayToPass: Know all sandbox types cold: Developer, Developer Pro, Partial Copy, and Full Copy — their data limits, refresh intervals, and the development phase each one serves.
Compare deployment tools: Understand the exact limitations of change sets (no delete, no version control) and when to recommend Salesforce CLI, MDAPI, or unlocked packages instead.
Study destructive changes: Know how destructiveChanges.xml works, what happens when you delete a field referenced by a validation rule, and how to plan safe metadata removal.
Design CI/CD pipelines: Practice designing a complete pipeline from Git commit through scratch org validation, test execution, and production deployment with approval gates.

certificationCard.description: This exam covers sandbox strategy, source-driven development, CI/CD pipelines, and package-based deployment on the Salesforce Platform. You'll need to choose between change sets and unlocked packages and design a release management process.

keyConcepts.h2: Development Lifecycle and Deployment Architect: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Org Strategy: Sandboxes and Scratch Orgs
blocks.body: Sandbox types: Developer (5 MB data, for development), Developer Pro (1 GB), Partial Copy (5 GB sample data, for integration testing), Full Copy (full production replica, for load and UAT testing). Scratch Orgs are temporary, source-driven orgs created from a definition file — ideal for CI/CD. The exam tests which sandbox type to use for each phase of development and when scratch orgs are preferred over traditional sandboxes.

blocks.heading: Version Control and Source-Driven Development
blocks.body: Salesforce DX uses a source format for metadata — different from the API (MDAPI) format used by Change Sets. .forceignore excludes files from source tracking (similar to .gitignore). Project Scratch Def files define scratch org configuration (edition, features, settings). sfdx project.json defines the package directories and plugin configuration. The exam tests source-driven development concepts, the difference between metadata formats, and how source tracking works in scratch orgs.

blocks.heading: CI/CD Pipelines: Salesforce CLI and Packages
blocks.body: Salesforce CLI (sf commands) drives automated deployments. Unlocked Packages are the recommended packaging model — versioned, installable, supports dependency management. Managed Packages are for ISVs distributing on **AppExchange** — locked source. The exam tests the deployment tool hierarchy: Change Sets (org-based, no version control) → Salesforce CLI & MDAPI (scriptable) → Unlocked Packages (modular, versioned). CI/CD tools (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, CircleCI) automate test runs and deployments on code push.

blocks.heading: Testing in the Deployment Pipeline
blocks.body: A minimum of 75% code coverage and all passing tests are required for production deployments. Test suites group related test classes. Run Specified Tests skips unrelated tests for faster deployments. Full test run is required for production. The exam tests how to structure test strategies — unit tests for individual classes, integration tests across objects, UAT in Partial/Full sandboxes. Test.isRunningTest() should not be used to bypass logic; instead design for testability.

blocks.heading: Release Management and Deployment Order
blocks.body: Destructive Changes (destructiveChanges.xml) remove components during deployment — must be planned carefully as deleted components cannot be recovered. Dependency order matters: deploy custom objects before fields, custom fields before **validation rules** referencing them. Rollback strategy: Salesforce does not have built-in rollback — plan with sandbox parity, feature flags, and version-controlled deployment scripts. Post-deployment verification should include running smoke tests and checking critical business processes. The exam tests deployment sequencing and risk mitigation strategies.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce Development Lifecycle and Deployment Architect Exam
scenarioTips.intro: The Dev Lifecycle Architect exam tests expertise in ALM, CI/CD, sandbox strategy, and package development. Focus on choosing the right deployment approach for complex org configurations and release management.

blocks.heading: Sandbox Strategy
blocks.body: Know the four sandbox types and when to use each: Developer (unit testing), Developer Pro (data load testing), Partial Copy (realistic data subset), Full (UAT with production data volume). Know refresh intervals.

blocks.heading: Change Set Limitations
blocks.body: Change sets have significant limitations: no delete capability, no metadata dependency resolution, no version control. Know when to move beyond change sets to source-driven development.

blocks.heading: Source-Driven Development
blocks.body: Understand SFDX / SF CLI source format, scratch orgs for isolated development, how to push/pull metadata, and how Salesforce DX integrates with Git version control systems.

blocks.heading: Package Development (2GP)
blocks.body: Know the difference between Unlocked Packages and Managed Packages. Understand how to define package boundaries, handle dependencies between packages, and version package releases.

blocks.heading: CI/CD Pipeline Design
blocks.body: Know how to design a CI/CD pipeline: source → scratch org → unit tests → package version → sandbox UAT → production. Understand how tools like GitHub Actions, Copado, or Gearset automate the pipeline.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the primary focus of a Development Lifecycle and Deployment Architect?
options: Assessing architecture environments and requirements to implement management solutions for deployment on the Salesforce Platform
sampleQuestions.explanation: They assess environments and implement management solutions for deployment.
whyWrong: 'Only coding' undersells the role, which is about assessing environments and deployment strategy, not just writing code.
Email is unrelated to the architect's core deployment management focus.
Slack is unrelated to the architect's core deployment management focus.

sampleQuestions.question: Which tool is used for source-driven deployments in Salesforce?
options: Salesforce CLI and source tracking (e.g., Salesforce DX)
sampleQuestions.explanation: Salesforce CLI and source tracking (e.g., Salesforce DX) support source-driven deployments.
whyWrong: Change Sets are a UI-based deployment tool, not the source-driven CLI approach the question asks about.
Data Loader moves records, not metadata/source code for deployments.
Workbench is a data/metadata utility tool, not the primary source-driven deployment tool described.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the purpose of Change Sets?
options: Moving metadata between orgs (e.g., sandbox to production)
sampleQuestions.explanation: Change Sets move metadata between orgs in deployment pipelines.
whyWrong: 'Only backup' misrepresents Change Sets' actual purpose, which is moving metadata between orgs, not backup.
'Only reports' is unrelated to what Change Sets do.
'Only dashboards' is unrelated to what Change Sets do.

sampleQuestions.question: Which environment is typically used for production-like testing?
options: Full Copy or Partial Copy sandbox
sampleQuestions.explanation: Full Copy or Partial Copy sandboxes provide production-like environments for testing.
whyWrong: A Developer org lacks the production-scale data and configuration needed for realistic testing.
Testing directly in Production defeats the purpose of a safe pre-production testing environment.
A Scratch org is typically used for short-lived development, not production-like data testing.

sampleQuestions.question: What does CI/CD mean in the context of Salesforce deployment?
options: Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment (automated build and release)
sampleQuestions.explanation: CI/CD automates build, test, and release for Salesforce metadata.
whyWrong: 'Only manual' is the opposite of what CI/CD automation represents.
'Only integration' undersells CI/CD, which covers both integration and deployment automation.
'Only deployment' undersells CI/CD, which spans both continuous integration and deployment.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a scratch org used for?
options: Temporary, configurable orgs for development and testing
sampleQuestions.explanation: Scratch orgs are temporary, configurable orgs for dev and testing.
whyWrong: Production deployment is the opposite of a scratch org's temporary development/testing purpose.
A Full Copy sandbox is a different, more persistent environment type than a scratch org.
'Data load only' misrepresents a scratch org's actual purpose as a temporary dev/test environment.

sampleQuestions.question: Which source control system integrates with Salesforce DX?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Salesforce DX is designed to work with Git and related tools.
whyWrong: 'None' contradicts the fact that Salesforce DX explicitly integrates with source control systems like Git.
SVN isn't the source control system commonly integrated with Salesforce DX — Git is.
TFVC isn't the source control system commonly integrated with Salesforce DX — Git is.

sampleQuestions.question: What does destructive change handling require?
options: destructiveChanges.xml or equivalent for metadata removal
sampleQuestions.explanation: destructiveChanges.xml specifies metadata to be removed.
whyWrong: 'No handling' contradicts the fact that destructive changes require specific handling via a manifest file.
'Only add' misrepresents destructive change handling, which is specifically about removing metadata, not adding it.
'Only update' misrepresents destructive change handling, which is about removal, not updates.

sampleQuestions.question: Which sandbox type best supports integration testing?
options: Partial Copy or Full Copy for data and integration testing
sampleQuestions.explanation: Partial/Full Copy sandboxes provide data for integration testing.
whyWrong: A Developer sandbox is too small in scope for realistic integration testing with production-like data.
A Scratch org is typically for short-lived development, not full-scale integration testing.
Testing directly in Production defeats the purpose of a safe pre-production testing environment.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the purpose of a release branch in CI/CD?
options: To isolate release-specific changes and promote to production
sampleQuestions.explanation: Release branches isolate and promote release-specific changes.
whyWrong: 'To replace main' misrepresents a release branch's purpose, which is to isolate changes, not replace the main branch.
'Only for development' undersells a release branch's specific promotion-to-production purpose.
'Only for testing' undersells a release branch's broader isolation-and-promotion purpose.

sampleQuestions.question: Which governance practice supports deployment quality?
options: Peer review, automated tests, and approval gates
sampleQuestions.explanation: Peer review, tests, and approval gates ensure quality.
whyWrong: 'No governance' contradicts the fact that peer review and approval gates are real governance practices.
'Manual only' undersells the automated testing and approval-gate components of good governance.
'No approval' contradicts the fact that approval gates are a core governance practice.

sampleQuestions.question: What does sf project deploy start do?
options: Deploys source from project to target org
sampleQuestions.explanation: sf project deploy start deploys source to target org.
whyWrong: 'Nothing' contradicts the fact that this command has a specific, real deployment function.
'Only retrieves' misrepresents the command's actual purpose, which is deploying (not retrieving).
'Only creates scratch org' misattributes this deployment command to an unrelated org-creation function.

sampleQuestions.question: Which deployment tool supports unlocked packages?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Salesforce CLI supports unlocked package development.
whyWrong: Change Sets alone don't support unlocked packages — that's a Salesforce CLI capability.
Data Loader is for data records, unrelated to deploying unlocked packages.
Workbench is a data/metadata utility, not the tool that supports unlocked package deployment.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the benefit of metadata API for deployment?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Metadata API enables programmatic deployment and retrieval.
whyWrong: 'No benefit' contradicts the real, documented benefits of the Metadata API for deployment.
'Manual only' is the opposite of the programmatic, scriptable nature the Metadata API provides.
'UI only' is the opposite of the API-driven, scriptable nature of the Metadata API.

sampleQuestions.question: Which best practice applies to release management?
options: Use sandbox promotion path and validate before production
sampleQuestions.explanation: Promote through sandboxes and validate before production.
whyWrong: Deploying directly to production skips the validation and testing sandbox promotion path best practice recommends.
'No testing' contradicts the core best practice of validating changes before production.
'Single environment only' contradicts the multi-stage sandbox promotion path this best practice recommends.
